Uganda Electricity Transmission Co Ltd Faces Insolvency, Disrupting National Grid Operations

Kampala – The Ugandan power sector was rattled this week as Uganda Electricity Transmission Co Ltd (UETCL), the state-owned electricity transmission operator, entered insolvency proceedings, sparking immediate concerns over the stability of the national grid and ongoing projects.

The insolvency process, confirmed by the Ministry of Energy and Mineral Development on Thursday, has already begun to impact UETCL’s day-to-day operations. Company sources report delays in critical maintenance work and in the execution of new infrastructure projects. “We are prioritizing essential repairs to keep power flowing, but several network upgrades and expansions have been put on hold,” an official within UETCL said, requesting anonymity as the situation evolves.

UETCL, responsible for the bulk transmission of electricity across Uganda, has long grappled with financial strains stemming from mounting debt and unpaid invoices from power distributors. The insolvency, which could lead to either administration or liquidation, is expected to complicate the company’s contractual obligations and threaten ongoing transmission line expansions, including the much-anticipated Northern Corridor link.

Industry observers warn that the uncertainty could have ripple effects across Uganda’s power supply chain. “Transmission is the backbone of the electricity sector. Any disruption here risks causing widespread outages or project delays,” noted Joseph Musoke, an analyst at Kampala Energy Insights. He added, “Independent power producers and construction contractors will be watching closely to see how the government responds.”

The Uganda Electricity Workers Union expressed concern for the company’s 1,200 employees, citing fears of unpaid wages and job losses. “Staff morale is low, and anxiety is high. Our members are essential workers keeping the grid operational under very difficult circumstances,” said union leader Sarah Nansubuga.

The Ministry of Energy has pledged to work with interim managers to ensure continued delivery of electricity transmission services. “Our priority is to stabilize the grid and protect critical infrastructure,” said a spokesperson.

As the insolvency proceedings unfold, stakeholders across Uganda’s power sector are bracing for further operational disruptions and awaiting clarity on the fate of UETCL’s assets and workforce.
